== Biography ==
James Dwyre Glasgow was born 4 Dec 1841in Adams County, Ohio.<ref>1860 United States Federal Census for James D Glasgow</ref> He was the son of [[Glasgow-2175|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Finley-4018|Mary Finley]]. 

In 1860 he graduated from Washington College in Washington, Iowa.<ref>Portrait and Biographical Album of Washington County, p 189</ref>

On 23 Jul 1860 he lived in Jackson Township, Washington County, Iowa.<ref>1860 United States Federal Census for James D Glasgow Iowa Washington Jackson</ref>

On 10 Aug 1861, during the Civil War, he enlisted from Iowa as a Private in the Eighth Regiment Iowa Infantry, Company C<ref>James D. Glasgow in the U.S., Civil War Soldiers, 1861-1865</ref>

{{US Civil War|side=USA}}

He was imprisoned by the CSA on 6 Apr 1862 in Shiloh, Tennessee.<ref>James D Gasglow in the U.S., Civil War Soldier Records and Profiles, 1861-1865</ref>

He was "exchanged at length, rejoined his regiment; died of disease at Pochahantas, Tennessee on 11 Feb 1863."<ref>Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Press, Inc., 1990), p 79</ref>
He was initially buried in Pocahontas, Tennessee, and then re-interred at Corinth National Cemetery in Corinth, Mississippi.<ref>James D Gasglow
in the U.S., Civil War Soldier Records and Profiles, 1861-1865</ref>
